key: must:J50b:Plane rests on notebook, not bare desk
symptom: Plane rests on notebook, not bare desk

whys.why: Why does no output show the plane resting on an open notebook?
whys.because: In both chats the only file graded is the turn-1 video. The turn-2 "notebook ending" was never generated.
whys.evidence: s2.new.happy.J50b/calls.jsonl: the only file is assets/01-wait_for_video_project.mp4, from the turn-1 create_video_from_text call whose prompt says "lands softly on a wooden desk". grade.json: "The plane rests directly on the wooden desk." s2r.new.stupid.J50b/grade.json: "the video is the unchanged original sky flight", "No landing at all". The stupid user's vague turn 1 got a sky-only prompt, so there was no landing to begin with.

whys.why: Why was no turn-2 video made in the happy chat?
whys.because: The assistant tried to cut seconds 0–5 with trim_video, but the server has no such tool. It then told the user that no tool can cut a video. The only option it could run, regenerating the whole video with edit_video, would not keep the first 5 s exactly, so the user refused it. The user also had no hand-trimmed clip to upload. The chat ended with the assistant waiting.
whys.evidence: s2.new.happy.J50b/calls.jsonl line 10: trim_video returned "Unknown tool: 'trim_video'". Line 13: "None of my tools can cut a video without changing it … I can only take the last frame." Line 14: the user says "Option 1 isn't what I want … I don't have a trimmed clip". Lines 17–24: no further tool calls.

whys.why: Why did the assistant believe trim_video existed, and why was there no other way to keep exactly seconds 0–5?
whys.because: The new build's plan_request lists trim_video as a valid tool, and plan_request even returned ready:true for it. But no trim_video tool is registered. The only frame tool is get_last_frame, which takes only the last frame. join_videos joins only whole videos. edit_video regenerates the frames it touches.
whys.evidence: tools-new.json: the plan_request "tool" enum includes "trim_video". No tool named trim_video exists in the list. get_last_frame: "Take the last frame of a video". join_videos: "Join videos end to end". edit_video: "Edits the appearance or content of a supplied video segment".

whys.why: Why was no turn-2 video made in the stupid chat, where the user accepted the whole-video regeneration?
whys.because: The harness refused the edit_video call because the free account had no credits left.
whys.evidence: s2r.new.stupid.J50b/calls.jsonl line 28: edit_video was refused with approve:false, reason "insufficient credits: this call needs about 192 credits and 0 remain on the account".

whys.why: Why were there no credits left?
whys.because: The first 8-second ltx-2.5 video at 480p cost 192 credits (24 per second), and that used up the whole free balance. The exact-preserve route would also have needed credits: the assistant quoted about 72 for a new 3-second ending. So on this account no turn-2 generation of any kind could run, even if a trim tool had existed.
whys.evidence: Both chats' calls.jsonl: create_video_from_text est/credits 192. Stupid chat: "0 remain" right after it. Happy chat line 17: "The new ending will cost about 72 credits." tools-new.json create_production_clip: "24 for each second at 480p".

whys.why: Why can't the system avoid this?
whys.because: This is the axiom. The free-plan credit budget pays for exactly one 8-second video, and this two-turn test needs a second, paid generation. The missing trim tool made it worse in the happy chat, but the budget alone blocks the notebook landing in both chats.
whys.evidence: The test J50b.json expects "beyond_free": "no", but turn 2 needs new frames, which always cost credits. The stupid chat shows the balance at 0 after turn 1.

result.axiom: The free-plan account has about 192 credits. The turn-1 8-second video (24 credits per second) uses all of them, so the notebook ending in turn 2 can never be generated. In the new build this combines with a tool gap: plan_request lists 'trim_video', but no such tool exists, and only last-frame extraction and whole-video joins are available. So the assistant could not even offer the exact keep-the-first-5-s path.
result.fix: There are two parts. (1) Add a free trim_video tool to the new build, or remove it from the plan_request enum. It should run server-side like join_videos (video id/URL plus start_seconds and end_seconds). Then the assistant can trim to 0–5 s, call get_last_frame, make a 3-second notebook landing from that frame with create_video_from_image, and join the two clips with join_videos. (2) That path still needs about 72 credits, and the free plan has none left after turn 1. So either fund the bench account for the second turn of multi-turn edit tests, or mark J50b as beyond_free. On the current free budget the turn-2 landing cannot be made.
